raw_case_text: A 65-year-old female, never smoker, with a history of hypertension, was diagnosed with colon cancer metastatic to the liver in June 2007. The patient commenced chemotherapy treatment according to the FOLFIRI protocol (bevacizumab/5-fluorouracil/irinotecan). From July 2007 to July 2009, she received 19 cycles of therapy with good response. Then she underwent liver metastasectomy and, in October 2009, she started chemotherapy according to the FOLFOX protocol (bevacizumab/5-fluorouracil/oxaliplatin). No treatment related side effects were noted and the patient was in very good performance status (WHO 1) until the 6th cycle of chemotherapy. On day 15 of the 6th cycle, she developed dyspnea and fever immediately after the treatment with oxaliplatin. She was treated with intravenous corticosteroids and promethazine with symptomatic improvement of the dyspnea. The following day her dyspnea worsened, with several episodes of near-syncope. Her saturation without oxygen was measured as low as 73%, and blood pressure was as low as 100/50 mm/Hg, but no tachycardia was observed. On physical examination, the patient was dyspneic, rales were heard on auscultation to the lungs, and mild pitting edema was noticed on the lower limbs. Initial blood tests revealed respiratory alkalosis, moderate acute-on-chronic renal failure, and hyponatremia of 122 mEq/L. Troponin and brain natriuretic peptide levels, as well as echocardiography, did not show cardiac failure or ischemia. Chest X-ray showed no pulmonary congestion (following treatment with loop diuretics) or infection. Chest CT scan showed diffused bilateral ground glass infiltrates and no pulmonary emboli (Figure 1). After ruling out cardiac and thromboembolic etiology of the dyspnea, diagnostic bronchoscopy was performed. Bronchoalveolar lavage analysis, along with blood cultures, revealed no sign of bacterial, viral, or Pneumocystis carinii infection, and no eosinophilia. Candida infection was present in fungal cultures. Pulmonary biopsy showed organizing diffuse alveolar damage. A diagnosis of interstitial pneumonitis was concluded, most probably drug-induced. The patient was treated with high-dose corticosteroids and wide ranging antibiotics, until the diagnosis of bacterial infection was ruled out, antifungal drugs, and loop diuretics. She received respiratory support with oxygen and continuous positive airway pressure. The patient's respiratory failure did not improve with treatment and she died 15 days following initial presentation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old female with metastatic colon cancer developed acute dyspnea and fever immediately after receiving her sixth cycle of FOLFOX plus bevacizumab chemotherapy, followed the next day by severe hypoxemia and near-syncope.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed in June 2007 with colon cancer metastatic to the liver, the patient received 19 cycles of FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab (July 2007 – July 2009) with good response, underwent hepatic metastasectomy, and started FOLFOX (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin) plus bevacizumab in October 2009. She maintained a WHO performance status of 1 without side effects through five cycles, but on day 15 of the 6th cycle she developed acute dyspnea and fever immediately after oxaliplatin infusion. Despite transient symptomatic relief with IV corticosteroids and promethazine, her dyspnea markedly worsened the next day with recurrent episodes of near-syncope.
subjective.past_medical_history: Colon adenocarcinoma with liver metastases (diagnosed June 2007, status post 19 cycles of FOLFIRI + bevacizumab and liver metastasectomy); hypertension; lifetime never-smoker.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for acute fever, severe progressive dyspnea, and near-syncope.

objective.physical_examination: On admission: Dyspneic, room-air oxygen saturation (SpO2) as low as 73%, blood pressure as low as 100/50 mmHg without tachycardia; pulmonary rales on chest auscultation; mild bilateral lower extremity pitting edema.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory tests: Respiratory alkalosis, moderate acute-on-chronic renal failure, and severe hyponatremia (serum sodium 122 mEq/L); normal cardiac troponin and brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels; negative blood cultures. Echocardiography: No cardiac failure or ischemia. Chest X-ray: No pulmonary congestion (after loop diuretics) or focal infection.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT scan: Diffuse bilateral ground-glass infiltrates without pulmonary embolism. Diagnostic bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and lung biopsy: BAL negative for bacterial, viral, and Pneumocystis carinii infection and negative for eosinophilia (fungal cultures grew Candida); lung biopsy histopathology demonstrated organizing diffuse alveolar damage (DAD).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Fatal oxaliplatin/FOLFOX-induced acute interstitial pneumonitis (organizing diffuse alveolar damage confirmed by lung biopsy; cardiac, thromboembolic, bacterial, viral, and Pneumocystis carinii etiologies excluded by echocardiography, chest CT, blood cultures, and BAL). Plan and clinical course: Managed with supplemental oxygen, continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), high-dose systemic corticosteroids, broad-spectrum empirical antibiotics, antifungal therapy (for BAL Candida), and loop diuretics. Despite intensive respiratory and anti-inflammatory support, her respiratory failure proved refractory and she died 15 days after initial presentation.
